boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Swift Creek record (May 9, 1864) in the Bermuda Hundred Campaign [May 1864]. Port Walthall Junction (VA047) precedes on May 6-7 and Chester Station (VA051) follows on May 10; the frozen description also includes the May 9 Fort Clifton gunboat action. Army-wide returns, the campaign-wide casualty return and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Divisions' and the live field zero. Humphreys says Butler moved out on May 9 with a large part of his command under Gillmore and Smith, and gives the army's present-for-duty returns (1,329 officers and 30,543 enlisted infantry; Kautz's 97 officers and 2,804 cavalry). Butler's May 9 telegram cites 1,700 cavalry advanced up the Peninsula and Kautz's 3,000 cavalry from Suffolk.
claims.rationale: Army-wide returns and cavalry figures for forces not engaged at Swift Creek; no Confederate figure for May 9 was inspected. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. NPS says a premature Confederate attack at Arrowfield Church was driven back with heavy losses but not followed up, and that the Fort Clifton gunboats were driven off. Butler's May 9 telegram claims a severe and well-contested fight in which he whipped the enemy and took many prisoners.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Butler's claim and the recorded inconclusive result are kept separately.

open_questions: Gillmore's, Smith's and Hinks's reports, the Tenth Corps regimental reports of May 9-10 (Nos. 12-44), Bushrod Johnson's and Fulkerson's reports (Nos. 95, 99), Hagood's May 9 paragraph (in the selected report, not used here under the three-family ceiling) and the naval reports on Fort Clifton remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; for this campaign it summarizes Smith's, Gillmore's and Weitzel's reports and quotes Beauregard's reports and telegrams, so it is not independent of the Beauregard family. Butler's telegrams and Hagood's, Barton's and Beauregard's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Part 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
